page.after:
What the differences mean

Each of these units mounts on the dash, runs CarPlay from your phone and records to a microSD card with built-in cameras. The price tag doesn't show how many of those cameras actually record. Dividing the price by the recording cameras and by screen size makes the difference clear:

  • Lamtto RC28: $139.99 ÷ 2 recording cameras = $70.00 per camera; $139.99 ÷ 10.25 in = $13.66 per inch.
  • Carpuride W903 (dual cameras): $249.99 ÷ 2 = $125.00 per camera; $249.99 ÷ 9.3 in = $26.88 per inch.
  • Carpuride W903S: $279.90 ÷ 3 = $93.30 per camera; $279.90 ÷ 9.3 in = $30.10 per inch.
  • Carpuride W903 (front camera): $219.99 ÷ 1 = $219.99 per camera; $219.99 ÷ 9.3 in = $23.65 per inch.
  • Rexing 6.86-inch: $159.99 ÷ 2 = $80.00 per camera if the rear records, and $159.99 if only the front does; $159.99 ÷ 6.86 in = $23.32 per inch.

Cost per recording camera: what the camera labels leave out

Carpuride sells the W903 with a front camera only for $219.99 and with front and rear cameras for $249.99, so the rear camera adds $249.99 − $219.99 = $30.00. That is also the price of Carpuride's separate wired rear camera for the W903. If you buy the front-only unit and add a rear camera later, it has to be the wired one: Carpuride states its WF01 wireless rear camera "cannot be used with Carpuride W903". The front-only listing caps the microSD card at 64 GB. The W903S takes up to 128 GB and includes a 64 GB card.

All W903 versions run on USB-C 5 V 2 A. Carpuride says to use its original car charger, "otherwise, will affect the FM transmission performance", which matters if your car has no AUX or Bluetooth and you play sound over FM. Carpuride also states that HarmonyOS phones and Huawei P and Mate series phones are not supported.

The 4K front camera doesn't start recording the moment you start the car. The Tiny Campervan's write-up of the Lens Of James video timed the W903 at 7 s to the home screen and 8 s more before the dash cam was recording, about 15 s in all, and 22 s from off to wireless Android Auto.

For a cheaper unit, ESSGOO's E64 10.26-inch CarPlay screen with a built-in 4K dash cam was $129.99 at essgoo.com on 2026-11-14. ESSGOO's product page wouldn't load for us, so we couldn't count its recording cameras, and it isn't in the table.

Not recommended

Rexing 6.86-inch CarPlay display with 4K dash cam. Target sells it for $159.99, and its highlights promise "4K+1080P Recording". In the same page's Q&A, one answer says "No. Only records front but it comes with a rear camera", and another gives the screen as 6.25 inches. If only the front records, that is $159.99 for one recording camera on the smallest screen here. Rexing's own store lists this model only as a sold-out open-box unit. Parking-mode recording needs Rexing's $29.99 FM Smart Hardwire Kit, which brings the total to $189.98. For front and rear recording, the Lamtto RC28 costs $20.00 less and has a 10.25-inch screen.
